name: Julia
title: Believing woman in Rome
summary: Julia was a Christian woman in the church at Rome whom Paul greets in his letter to the Romans. She is mentioned together with Philologus, suggesting that they were spouses or close family members. She was part of the early Christian movement in the capital of the Roman Empire.

keyEvents.title: Greeting from Paul
keyEvents.description: Paul greets Julia along with Philologus, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas in his letter to the Romans. This shows that she was a recognized part of the Christian community in Rome.

keyEvents.title: Part of the house churches in Rome
keyEvents.description: Julia was connected to one of the house churches in Rome, where the first Christians gathered for worship and fellowship before they had their own church buildings.
